title: One Hundred Lockers
problem: One hundred closed lockers are numbered 1 through 100. On pass k, you toggle every locker whose number is divisible by k. After passes 1 through 100, which lockers are open?

hints.text: Locker n is toggled once for every positive divisor of n.
Divisors normally come in distinct pairs d and n/d. Determine when one divisor is left unpaired.

solution.setup: A locker finishes open exactly when it is toggled an odd number of times.
solution.reasoning: Locker n is toggled on precisely the passes corresponding to divisors of n. Divisors pair as d and n/d, so non-square numbers have an even number of divisors. Perfect squares have one unpaired divisor, sqrt(n), and therefore an odd number of divisors. The open lockers are exactly the squares not exceeding 100.
solution.sanityCheck: Locker 12 is toggled on passes 1,2,3,4,6,12—six times—while locker 16 is toggled on 1,2,4,8,16—five times.

keyInsight: Only the parity of the number of toggles matters, and perfect squares are exactly the integers with an odd divisor count.
recognitionCues: Repeated toggling suggests tracking parity rather than simulating the full state.
commonMistakes: Assuming frequently toggled lockers stay open without checking whether the toggle count is odd or even.
followUps: How many lockers remain open if there are n lockers?

source.notes: Original exposition of the classical locker invariant puzzle.

verification.notes: Exactly floor(sqrt(100)) perfect squares remain open.
